events.title: Henry Hudson Begins Exploring the Hudson River
events.description: Sailing aboard the Halve Maen for the Dutch East India Company, English explorer Henry Hudson began his exploration of the river that now bears his name.
events.significance: His voyage underpinned Dutch claims in the region and led to the colony of New Netherland, which later became New York.

events.title: Battle of Vienna
events.description: Polish troops led by King John III Sobieski joined a Habsburg-led coalition army. Together they defeated the besieging Ottoman forces outside Vienna.
events.significance: The victory marked a turning point in the Great Turkish War. It ended the Ottoman Empire's advance into central Europe.

events.title: Lascaux Cave Paintings Discovered
events.description: Four teenagers exploring near Montignac in France's Dordogne region found a cave filled with Paleolithic paintings. The art is estimated to be about 17,000 years old.
events.significance: Lascaux is one of the most celebrated examples of prehistoric art. It gave modern people a vivid view of Ice Age human creativity.

events.title: Jack Kilby Demonstrates the First Integrated Circuit
events.description: Working at Texas Instruments, engineer Jack Kilby demonstrated the first working integrated circuit. It put multiple electronic components on a single piece of semiconductor material.
events.significance: The invention paved the way for modern microchips, computers and smartphones. It earned Kilby a share of the 2000 Nobel Prize in Physics.

events.title: Emperor Haile Selassie I Is Deposed
events.description: Ethiopia's Emperor Haile Selassie I was removed from power by the Derg, a military junta, after months of unrest.
events.significance: His fall ended one of the world's oldest monarchies, which had lasted for centuries. It ushered in a period of military rule in Ethiopia.
